questions.question: What is a LinkedList?
explanations: Correct. LinkedList is a doubly linked list where each element has a reference to the previous and the next one.
No. LinkedList is doubly linked, not singly.
No. It is not an array; it is a collection of linked nodes.
No. Although it can be used as FIFO, its definition is a doubly linked list.

questions.question: What advantage does LinkedList have over ArrayList?
options: Efficient insertion and removal at the ends
explanations: Correct. LinkedList is more efficient for insertions and removals at the ends of the list.
No. ArrayList has better random access because it uses an internal array.
No. LinkedList uses more memory because of the node references.
No. LinkedList does not automatically sort elements.

questions.question: How do you add an element to the beginning of a LinkedList?
explanations: Correct. The addFirst() method adds an element to the beginning of the LinkedList.
No. Although add(0, element) works, addFirst() is more semantic and efficient.
No. There is no insertFirst() method in LinkedList.
No. There is no prepend() method in LinkedList.

questions.question: How do you remove the last element of a LinkedList?
explanations: Correct. The removeLast() method removes and returns the last element of the LinkedList.
No. remove() without parameters removes the first one, not the last.
No. There is no deleteLast() method in LinkedList.
No. There is no popLast() method in LinkedList.
